data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists reveal what seven days of fasting does to the human body

data.title: ScienceDaily: Vagus Nerve Stimulation Could Help New Skills Stick
data.summary: Stimulating the vagus nerve after practice helped mice develop stronger long-term motor learning, revealing a potentially important window when the brain is still locking in a new skill. The effect was linked to rhythmic changes in brain blood vessels, hinting that body-to-brain signals may help prepare the brain for lasting change.

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists just found a way to fight lung cancer and muscle wasting at the same time
data.summary: A new nanoparticle therapy reduced lung tumors in mice while also targeting cachexia, the severe muscle wasting that can accompany cancer. By delivering follistatin mRNA directly to tumors, the approach could eventually offer a way to fight both the disease and one of its most dangerous complications.

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists discover a human brain gene that can jump through DNA
data.summary: Scientists have discovered a human gene with a remarkable double life: it appears to play an important role in brain cells while still retaining the ability to jump around the genome. Called BC200, the gene evolved millions of years ago from a mobile piece of DNA known as a transposon, but unlike most genes that arose this way, it never lost its mobility. Researchers even found BC200 embedded inside a human poxvirus, suggesting it may have jumped from infected skin cells into the virus.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists discover a human brain gene that can jump through DNA

data.title: ScienceDaily: Cancer-fighting t cells burn out. Scientists may have found a fix
data.summary: Cancer immunotherapy can lose its punch when tumor-fighting T cells become exhausted, but researchers may have found a way to keep them going longer. Scientists at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center identified a signaling molecule called MEK that can push T cells to burn through their energy while producing cancer-killing proteins. In animal and laboratory studies, blocking MEK helped the cells conserve energy, survive longer, and remain active even in the harsh environment around tumors.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Cancer-fighting t cells burn out. Scientists may have found a fix

data.title: ScienceDaily: This mysterious hole on the Moon may open into a giant cave
data.summary: NASA has selected the GIMLI project to investigate whether the Marius Hill Pit opens into a vast underground cave or lava tube. Using radar, seismic sensors, gravity measurements, and cameras, researchers will search beneath the lunar surface and estimate the size of any hidden void. Such caves could preserve clues to the Moon’s volcanic history and potentially provide protected shelters for future astronauts.
